edge_cases: Missing or empty form fields may cause a server error or unexpected behavior.
Database connection failures or query errors will abort the request without a defined response.
SQL injection is possible because user input is concatenated directly into SQL statements.
If the generated session_id collides with an existing one, the insert may fail.
Very large input values could exceed database column limits or cause performance issues.
contract.intent: Register a new user account via a POST request and create a session for the user.
invariants: A username must be unique; duplicate usernames are rejected.
The password is always stored as a bcrypt hash, never in plain text.
All required environment variables for database connection must be present.
A session_id of exactly 16 alphanumeric characters is generated for each new registration.
io_behavior: Accepts a POST request to /register with form fields: username, password, name, email, cweid.
On success, responds with an HTTP redirect to /login including username, session_id, and stake as query parameters.
On failure due to an existing username, responds with the plain text message "Username is already taken".
side_effects: Inserts a new row into the users table with the supplied data and a bcrypt‑hashed password.
Creates a new session record in the sessions table containing a generated session_id.
Commits the above inserts to the MySQL database.

rationale: Program fulfills main intent, I/O contract, side‑effects and invariants, but mitigates the listed SQL‑injection edge case, deviating from the contract; other edge cases are present.
